framework_rationale: The board is asked to approve a specific proposal; Situation-Complication-Resolution lets us state the proposal, show where its saving and risk case break (problem and risk first), then resolve with an approvable alternative.

candidates.text: Reject the 100% move to Supplier B and approve a 70/30 split: the full move's real saving is €2.87M a year, not €3.0M, and a repeat of Supplier B's two stoppages (€4.0M) would wipe out the €2.93M it adds over the split, which nets €4.88M over 2026-2028 and keeps a second plant
Approve the move to Supplier B but correct the saving to €2.87M a year and add a business-continuity plan
Keep both suppliers as today until the rush-freight problem is solved

governing_thought: Reject the 100% move to Supplier B and approve a 70/30 split instead: the full move's real saving is €2.87M a year, not €3.0M, and a repeat of Supplier B's two stoppages (€4.0M) would wipe out the €2.93M it adds over the split, which saves €1.79M a year, nets €4.88M over 2026-2028 and keeps a second plant.

key_line.message: Procurement's €3.0M a year is overstated: 12% cannot apply to €1.1M of rush freight, so the full move saves €2.87M a year gross, €7.80M over 2026-2028 after €0.8M switching
Single-sourcing on Supplier B's one plant is the bigger issue: its two stoppages in three years would cost €4.0M with all volume on it, more than the €2.93M the full move adds over a 70/30 split
A 70/30 split saves €1.79M a year and nets €4.88M over 2026-2028, ahead of the full move's €3.80M once stoppage risk is counted
The remaining gap to €3.0M sits in our own forecasting: €0.65M of €1.1M rush freight falls in months flagged as our forecast errors

target.statement: Procurement's claimed annual saving from packaging sourcing

levers.statement: Move Supplier B to 70% of volume at its 9% price tier
levers.validate: Supplier B confirms the 9% tier at 70% for 2026-2028 in writing, before contract signature (Q4 2026)

levers.statement: Keep the incumbent at 30% of volume with its offered 4% price reduction
levers.validate: Incumbent's 4% offer at 30% volume confirmed in a 2026-2028 contract (Q4 2026)

gap.how_closed: Not closed by price: the extra €1.08M a year (C0012) is only available through 100% single sourcing, which a repeat of Supplier B's stoppages (€1.33M a year on average, C0005) outweighs. The only further lever is rush freight (€1.1M a year, F0055), driven by our own forecast errors; its reducible share is an upper bound to be sized by a demand-planning review before any of it is booked.

current_plan.statement: Procurement proposal: move 100% of packaging to Supplier B from January 2026 under a three-year commitment, saving €3.0M a year

cost_if_kept.statement: Three-year shortfall versus the 70/30 split if Supplier B's stoppage record repeats (€3.80M vs €4.88M net), plus an uncovered single-plant exposure

options.statement: Keep today's 70/30 incumbent/Supplier B split without renegotiation: no saving, no switching cost
Procurement's full move to Supplier B: €7.80M net over 2026-2028 before risk, €3.80M if the stoppage record repeats; one-off switching cost €0.8M
Flip to 70% Supplier B / 30% incumbent: €4.88M net over 2026-2028, second plant retained; one-off switching cost €0.5M

asks.statement: Reject procurement's proposal to move 100% of packaging to Supplier B
Approve a 70% Supplier B / 30% incumbent split for 2026-2028, with a €0.5M one-off switching budget
Commission a demand-planning review to size and cut the €1.1M of rush freight

gates.criterion: Supplier B 9% tier at 70% and incumbent 4% at 30% both signed for 2026-2028; otherwise return to the board
Incumbent ramp-up plan to cover Supplier B's share in a stoppage tested, and Supplier B force-majeure root causes reviewed
Reconsider 100% Supplier B only if it qualifies a second plant or the continuity plan covers a 14-day stoppage
